clue.text: Rushes to restrain company from punishing cats

definitions.note: cats here are cat-o'-nine-tails, whips used for punishment; plural noun phrase

indicators.note: to restrain something is to hold it in, so the word for rushes holds the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: rushes, as a crowd or water does, means surges

explanation.surface: Someone rushes in to stop a company from mistreating its cats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punishing cats' looks like cruelty to animals, but a cat here is the cat-o'-nine-tails, a many-tailed whip.
explanation.definitionFit: Whips used to flog people are lashes, and the cat-o'-nine-tails was the classic naval lash.

clue.text: A means of getting into port

definitions.text: A means of getting into port

parts.words: A means of getting into port
parts.note: port reads as a harbour, but it is the fortified wine, and the means of getting into it is the tool that draws the bottle's stopper

explanation.surface: Something that lets a ship enter a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiral tool pulls the stopper from a wine bottle, which is how a drinker gets at the port inside.

clue.text: Loosen international agency's restriction

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, is the best-known international agency
a tie is something that restricts or binds you

explanation.surface: An international body relaxes one of its rules.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo a knot or fastening is to slacken what was bound.

clue.text: Purveyor who is environmentally aware?

parts.note: environmentally aware means green in the eco sense, and a purveyor is a seller; together a green seller is a shopkeeper selling fruit and vegetables

explanation.surface: A trader with ecological credentials.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper selling fresh fruit and vegetables, punningly the green sort of seller.

clue.text: Expressed doubts following dismissal of this music-maker

indicators.note: following means the piece for doubts comes after the piece for dismissal

parts.note: getting the sack is being dismissed from a job
to but is to raise objections, as in 'no ifs or buts'

explanation.surface: Someone voiced reservations after a musician was fired.
explanation.walkthrough: A SACKBUT is an early trombone, a Renaissance brass instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument is something that makes music, and this one is an early trombone.

clue.text: Water jump

definitions.meaning: a source of water rising from the ground

explanation.definitionFit: A natural source where groundwater wells up; also a sudden leap.

clue.text: That volatile little girl

definitions.meaning: the word that goes before volatile in ... volatile, smelling salts
a pet form of Sally or Sarah

explanation.definitionFit: Sal volatile is smelling salts, and Sal is a diminutive girl's name.

clue.text: Bearded tits — single red variety

indicators.note: a variety is a different version, so these letters are rearranged into a new form

explanation.surface: Birdwatchers spot a lone red form of bearded tit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' turns SINGLE RED into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearded tits are small reed-bed birds, also called bearded reedlings.

clue.text: Pleasant to see Henry in the recess

indicators.note: in places the letter for Henry inside the word for pleasant

parts.note: pleasant means nice
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: It is nice to find Henry sitting in the alcove.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcove or hollow set into a wall is a small recess.

clue.text: Sort of saw for pine

definitions.meaning: a fretsaw is a fine-bladed saw for cutting curves
to pine is to worry or grieve

explanation.definitionFit: The first word of a fine-bladed saw's name; also to worry anxiously, as pining does.

clue.text: Ambassadorial quality

parts.note: an ambassador is addressed as Your Excellency, so the quality suited to one is that title's near-twin, meaning superiority

explanation.surface: The fine trait a diplomat should have.
explanation.definitionFit: Supreme merit, and the word behind the honorific Your Excellency given to ambassadors.

clue.text: A fox-hound's tail at the vessel's rear

parts.note: in hunting, a hound's tail is called its stern

explanation.surface: A hound's tail is seen at the back of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The stern is the hunting term for a foxhound's tail; the surface plays on the ship's stern too.
explanation.definitionFit: Behind a ship, towards or at its back end.

clue.text: One who observes there's liquor in the hold? To the contrary!

indicators.note: in, with the reversal note that follows, says one piece sits inside the other
to the contrary says the containment is the other way round: the hold goes inside the liquor

parts.note: beer is a liquor in the broad sense of an alcoholic drink
the hold, taken as written, gives its own word

explanation.surface: A watcher notes there is drink stored in a ship's hold.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface puts the drink inside the hold, but 'To the contrary!' swaps the roles, so the hold sits inside the liquor, with 'in' signalling the containment.
explanation.definitionFit: A watcher or onlooker, as in 'beauty is in the eye of'.

clue.text: GP healed the sick, for charity

indicators.note: something sick is out of order, so these letters are disordered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A doctor cured the ill, all for a good cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sick' rearranges GP HEALED THE. Help the Aged was a well-known British charity for older people.
explanation.definitionFit: A British charity for older people, now part of Age UK.

clue.text: Congress before the match? Later I will need pram wheeled out!

indicators.note: a pram wheeled out is moved about, so the letters are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A young couple's plans: a pram can come later, after the wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wheeled out' rearranges LATER, I and PRAM. Congress here means sex, and the match is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexual intercourse before marriage is the classic premarital sort.

clue.text: Aim to grit roundabout for someone seeking easier route

indicators.note: roundabout means going round in circles, so the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A council worker plans to salt the traffic circle for drivers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roundabout' rearranges AIM TO GRIT; grit and a roundabout belong to winter roads in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: One who makes things less harsh or severe, easing the way.

clue.text: Yard vehicle withdrawn from fleet

indicators.note: withdrawn means drawn back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A dockyard van is taken out of service with the fleet.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation's sea force, its fleet of warships.

clue.text: Almost give up weapon, I admit, keeping watch

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the letter for I goes inside the rest
up in a down clue means the letters read upwards, backwards
almost means the word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: taken as written, before trimming
a lance is a weapon

explanation.surface: A soldier half-surrenders a weapon while guarding the gate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts the last letter from give, 'up' reads the rest upwards as in a down clue, and 'admit' lets I into the middle of that run plus the weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Watchfulness is the state of being alert on guard.

clue.text: Directions with a tin-opener -— strike smartly

parts.note: S and W are the compass directions south and west

indicators.note: an opener is the first part, so take the first letter of tin

explanation.surface: Instructions come with a can-opener on how to hit it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opener' takes T, the first letter of tin.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit sharply, like flattening a fly.

clue.text: Excellent in parts?

parts.note: a Punch cartoon has a timid clergyman assuring his bishop that a bad boiled egg is good in parts; the phrase now means something of mixed quality

explanation.surface: A review praising only some sections.
explanation.walkthrough: From a famous Punch cartoon: a nervous young clergyman, served a bad egg by his bishop, says 'parts of it are excellent'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names something partly good and partly bad, like the clergyman's spoilt breakfast.

clue.text: The noise subsides but the hooligans making it remain

parts.note: a row is a loud noise or din
dies, as in dies down, means subsides

explanation.surface: The racket fades, but those who caused it stay.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'row dies', the noise subsides; the troublemakers remain in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough, noisy people who cause disorder.

clue.text: Sliced wedge — half hour finding ball here

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Sliced wedge — half hour finding ball here' gives WEDGE plus half of HOUR (HO or UR), but HEDGEROW needs WEDGE plus H, O, R; no parse found and no source to confirm the printed wording.
annotationWithheld.clue: Sliced wedge — half hour finding ball here

clue.text: Fit of pique

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Fit of pique': FIT must be both the definition (equip) and the anagram indicator for PIQUE, one word doing two jobs.

clue.text: Make mummy bring me back some ointment

indicators.note: back means the little word is turned round

parts.note: a balm is a soothing ointment

explanation.surface: Fetch me some cream, mum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ME to EM. Mummy is an Egyptian mummy, not mother.
explanation.definitionFit: To preserve a corpse with spices, as the Egyptians did.

clue.text: Such joy, to be a composer

definitions.meaning: Sir Arthur ..., English composer and Master of the Queen's Music

explanation.definitionFit: Perfect happiness; also the surname of the English composer Sir Arthur.

clue.text: Supporting American retreat on pollution?

indicators.note: to retreat is to go back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: US stands for American, as in US forces
staining is dirtying or polluting

explanation.surface: America backs down on its policy on pollution.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding up or upholding, as a sustaining diet keeps you going.

clue.text: Is ring concealed in this place?

indicators.note: concealed means the ring is hidden away within the other word

parts.note: O is shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: Is a ring hidden somewhere around here?
explanation.walkthrough: IOS is a small Greek island in the Cyclades.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek island, so a place one can be in.

clue.text: You'll hear I possess a small island

indicators.note: you'll hear says the words are spoken out loud and sound like the answer

parts.note: I possess a means I own a

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that they own a little island.
explanation.walkthrough: Iona is a small island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hebridean isle off Mull, famous for its abbey.

clue.text: Rejects incentives Poles without capital needed

indicators.note: without capital means a letter S, an upper-case capital in the surface sense of money, is removed

parts.note: spurs are incentives
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Polish workers turn down incentives because they lack funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without capital' is loose: one S of the incentives goes, then the two Poles follow; the surface's lack of funds is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn down with contempt is to reject.

clue.text: Seen in church when members of jazz group hold last rites?

indicators.note: to hold is to contain, so the jazz players surround the letter

parts.note: sidemen are the supporting players in a jazz band

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the word rites

explanation.surface: Jazz musicians conduct a funeral service.
explanation.walkthrough: Sidesmen are church officers who help ushers and take the collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Lay helpers in an Anglican church, ushering and collecting.
